articles.title: Puka Nacua injury update: Rams star wideout expected to be a game-time decision, but is reportedly 'trending in the wrong direction' due to hip and groin injuries
articles.summary: Puka Nacua did not practice Friday or Saturday due to hip and groin issues.
articles.body:
Coming off a surprising loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Los Angeles Rams need to bounce back against the New York Giants in Week 2 to live up to their status as Super Bowl contenders. But that task could prove difficult, as star wideout Puka Nacua will reportedly be a game-time decision who is " trending in the wrong direction " for Monday's game due to hip and groin injuries, per ESPN.

After a modest performance in the team's 27-7 loss to the 49ers, in which he caught five passes for 74 yards, Nacua was able to get on the practice field Thursday. But the wideout unexpectedly did not practice Friday, with head coach Sean McVay saying Nacua "didn't feel totally like himself" during Thursday's practice. The Rams eventually listed Nacua on the team's injury report with a hip issue.

After Nacua failed to practice Saturday, McVay added another ailment to the list, saying Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" to his groin, per ESPN. Despite not practicing both days, Nacua was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report.

While a questionable designation often results in a player trying to gut it out, McVay said Saturday that Nacua would be a true game-time decision in Week 2, per ESPN.

"Whether or not he plays is to be determined," McVay said. "And so we'll see how he's feeling."

It's a concerning development for Nacua, who — on top of playing Monday night — already had additional days to recover following the team's Week 1 game against the 49ers. That game aired Thursday night in the United States, giving Nacua a full 10 days to rest up for Week 2.

When healthy, Nacua is considered one of the best receivers in football. After gaining 1,715 receiving yards and scoring 10 touchdowns last season, Nacua was named a first-team All-Pro for the first time in his career.

The 25-year-old has battled minor injuries and ailments since being drafted in 2023. A knee issue caused Nacua to miss five games in 2024 and an ankle issue forced him to miss a game last season. He's popped up on the injury report other times, but has usually played through issues.

Who would replace Puka Nacua for Rams in Week 2?

If Nacua is unable to go in Week 1, veteran Davante Adams would serve as the team's de-facto No. 1 option against the Giants. Jordan Whittingham and Tutu Atwell could also see increased snaps if Nacua is out. The team could also feature tight end Terrance Ferguson more as a pass catcher if Nacua is unable to do his usual middle-of-the-field work.

Regardless of Nacua's status, the Rams need to turn in a much better performance in Week 2. After a listless outing in Week 1, the Rams can't afford to open the year 0-2, not when the team entered the year as one of the Super Bowl favorites.

articles.title: From a $15M divorce to a secret newborn at 54: Michael Strahan has everything except a reason to ever get married again
articles.summary: NFL News: Michael Strahan’s personal life has taken another turn at 54. The former NFL star and *Good Morning America* co-anchor is now a father of five after r.
articles.body: Michael Strahan’s personal life has taken another turn at 54. The former NFL star and *Good Morning America* co-anchor is now a father of five after reportedly welcoming a baby girl with longtime girlfriend Kayla Quick earlier this year. The news came weeks before Strahan opened up about marriage and admitted he is unsure about walking down the aisle again. After two marriages, a broken engagement and a costly divorce involving Jean Muggli, Strahan says he still believes in love, but his latest comments suggest marriage is no longer something he feels he needs to pursue.Why is Michael Strahan unsure about getting married again?Michael Strahan was asked directly about marriage during a recent interview with *Playboy*, and his answer was hardly a firm yes or no.“Would I get married again? Let’s not go there,” he joked during the interview. “Why you gonna put me on the spot like that?”He then left the door open without suggesting he was actively planning another wedding.“I’ll never say never,” continued Strahan. “I love love. Sometimes love doesn’t love me back.”The comments carry more weight given his history. Strahan has been married twice. His first marriage, to Wanda Hutchins, lasted from 1992 to 1996. He later married Jean Muggli in 1999, with the couple eventually divorcing in 2006. He was also engaged to Nicole Murphy, with that relationship ending in 2014. PEOPLE reported at the time that distance and demanding work schedules contributed to their split.What happened in Michael Strahan’s $15 million divorce?Strahan’s divorce from Muggli became one of the most expensive chapters of his personal life. In 2007, a judge awarded Muggli a reported $15 million divorce settlement, with Strahan also ordered to pay $18,000 a month in child support. Some later reports put the settlement at $15.3 million.The former couple share twin daughters, Isabella and Sophia, who are now 21. Strahan also has two older children, Tanita and Michael Jr., from his first marriage to Hutchins.That history helps explain why marriage may not carry the same appeal for him today. Still, Strahan has not said that he has rejected marriage permanently. His own words are more measured. He says he loves love and refuses to completely close the door.Who is Michael Strahan’s girlfriend Kayla Quick?Strahan has been linked to Kayla Quick since 2015, but the couple has kept much of their relationship away from public view. They rarely appear together and have not publicly detailed how they first met. Quick is also a co-founder of wellness company FIZZNESS.In August, PEOPLE reported that Strahan and Quick had welcomed their first child together. TMZ was first to report that the baby girl was born earlier in 2026. That made her Strahan’s fifth child.The timing makes his marriage comments particularly interesting, but there is no indication from Strahan that becoming a father again has changed his view of marriage.For now, his priorities appear to be family, work and the life he has built outside the NFL. Strahan has previously spoken about feeling happy and fortunate with the people around him. At 54, he does not appear eager to force his personal life into a familiar script just because marriage is expected to be the next step.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colts WR Keenan Allen facing at least a 3-game suspension following August drunk-driving arrest
articles.summary: The 34-year-old is expected to still play in Sunday night's game against the Chiefs.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was charged this week with two misdemeanor offenses stemming from his drunk-driving arrest on August 30.

A violation of the league's substance-abuse policy, which this was, comes with a minimum three-game suspension under the current NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement. A longer suspension can be issued if the player was more intoxicated.

Allen blew a .224 when he was arrested, nearly triple the legal limit of .08. His blood alcohol level was so high that it actually triggered a more serious Class A misdemeanor according to Indiana law.

The NFL is reportedly waiting for the legal proceedings of the case to conclude before issuing a suspension. Allen and the Colts will play the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2's "Sunday Night Football" game, despite the looming suspension.

The next aspect of Allen's case is expected to be an attorney conference on Oct. 26. This would mean that, at the earliest, the wide receiver's suspension could begin in Week 8 if the NFL does indeed wait for the situation to play out in the legal system.

The 34-year-old veteran was arrested at the end of August. He was initially charged with "operating a vehicle with alcohol concentration equivalent to .15 or more, and operating a vehicle while intoxicated." Both of these charges are misdemeanors.

Allen joined the Colts on a one-year deal. In his debut with the team in Week 1, he came down with all six of his targets for 32 yards.

The veteran wide receiver spent the 2025 season with the Los Angeles Chargers . Allen began his career with the franchise and played 11 years in San Diego and L.A. before leaving for the Chicago Bears for the 2024 season.

In 172 career games, Allen has tallied 12,083 yards with 70 touchdowns. He was expected to add a veteran presence to the Colts' receiving corps alongside Alec Pierce and Josh Downs . Now, Indianapolis awaits to see when, and for how long, it will lose Allen to a suspension.

articles.title: Steelers want Joey Porter Jr. to return in Week 3, but cornerback reportedly still struggling with back injury
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. will miss at least two games as he ramps back up after missing most of training camp.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers picked up a win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1 despite missing one of the team's most important defensive players. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out for that contest due to back and conditioning issues. While Porter participated in limited practices in Week 2, he'll miss Sunday's contest at the New England Patriots due to those issues.

If the team has its way, Porter will take the field next week. The Steelers are reportedly planning for Porter to return to action against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3.

Whether Porter actually takes the field, however, is an open question … both due to his back injury and — possibly — his contract situation, per ESPN .

But whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level. Porter's back, according to a source, has "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be." Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back.

But whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level.

Porter's back, according to a source, has "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be." Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back.

Porter — who is in the final year of his rookie contract — missed time early in training camp due to the situation. While he was able to return to practices ahead of the regular season, Porter was deemed to be in a "ramp-up" situation thanks to a back injury and his conditioning.

Despite practicing in a limited capacity each day leading up to Week 1, Porter did not play in the contest. Similarly, Porter was able to get in limited practice ahead of Week 2. This time around, however, the team ruled him out on its final injury report. That wasn't the case ahead of Week 1, when Porter was listed as "questionable" on the final injury report.

It's unclear when or how the situation will resolve itself. If Porter is truly plagued by a back issue, then the cornerback could miss additional weeks recovering from the injury. If his continued absences are related to Porter's contract situation, that could also cause issues, as the team has a long-standing policy of not negotiating contracts during the regular season.

If the team changes its mind, the framework for a deal is fairly obvious. In early September, the New England Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension that made Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in the league. Porter would — almost certainly — look to match or exceed that figure with his next contract.

Should Porter continue to sit out, a trade could wind up being the most likely outcome. The Steelers have reportedly entertained the idea, but are seeking a first-round pick in the deal, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor. That ask has reportedly scared teams off.

Porter's price could fall the longer the cornerback misses time. If that's the case, a trade could wind up being the best thing for both sides.

That scenario could potentially be avoided if Porter's back is OK and he returns to action in Week 3. That makes the upcoming week a big deal for both sides.

articles.title: How Gisele Bündchen walking away became the defining moment of Tom Brady's final and most painful NFL season
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady spent 23 years outrunning pressure, reading defenses, and delivering in the moments that mattered most. But during a recent appearance on Fo.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent 23 years outrunning pressure, reading defenses, and delivering in the moments that mattered most. But during a recent appearance on Fox Sports' The Herd, the seven-time Super Bowl champion admitted something no highlight reel ever captured: his 2022 season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the last of his career, was shaped far more by what was happening at home than anything that unfolded on the field. His marriage to Gisele Bündchen was falling apart. Publicly. Painfully. Right in the middle of a season he couldn't walk away from.Why did Tom Brady's divorce from Gisele Bündchen affect his performance on the field?There's a reason the 2022 season felt different. Tom Brady posted an 8-9 record that year, the only losing season of his entire career. Statistically, he still threw for 4,694 yards with 25 touchdowns. The numbers weren't embarrassing. But anyone who watched closely knew something was off.Gisele Bündchen had made her feelings about his return to the NFL very clear. After Brady announced his retirement in February 2022, only to reverse that decision weeks later, reports emerged that she was deeply unhappy about it. By October, the divorce was official. She filed. He kept playing. And every Sunday, Brady was suiting up for the Buccaneers while his 13-year marriage was dissolving in the tabloids and courtrooms."My last season was tough," Brady told The Herd. "I was going through — I had a lot of, you know, just a personal, family issue, and it was a challenge. It was very ... it just took a lot out of me in terms of, you know, my ability to continue to play."That's about as candid as Brady gets.Did Tom Brady's decision to un-retire cost him his marriage to Gisele Bündchen?It's hard to say it was one decision alone, but the unretirement certainly lit the fuse. Bündchen had reportedly grown frustrated with football for years, not just the time it consumed but the physical toll it was taking. She shared publicly that she worried about his long-term health. Two children at home. A life she wanted him to be present for.When Brady walked back his retirement, it sent a clear signal about where his priorities still sat. Their separation quietly began during preseason. Brady took a mysterious 10-day leave from Buccaneers training camp that August and nobody explained why. He later hinted at personal struggles. By the time October came, the divorce was filed and confirmed.He was 45, playing in his 23rd NFL season, while the marriage he had built over 13 years was ending. That is not a small thing to carry into a huddle on a Sunday afternoon.What did Tom Brady say about his regrets and moving on after the Gisele Bündchen divorce?Brady didn't dwell in self-pity during his comments on The Herd. If anything, he framed it with the same controlled restraint he brought to every fourth quarter he ever played. He acknowledged the difficulty but didn't point fingers or assign blame."I felt like I always had a goal — 45," he said. "I was 45 years old, I wanted to spend time with my kids. I felt like, okay, now it's time for me to be at all my kids' games. They've been to enough of their dad's games."He and Bündchen share two children together, Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. Brady also has an 18-year-old son, Jack, from his previous relationship with actress Bridget Moynihan. The divorce was finalized amicably, with both issuing statements about co-parenting and moving forward.But reading between the lines of what he said on The Herd, there's an honest reckoning there. Brady chose one more season of football. It cost him his marriage. And now, three years removed from all of it, he's saying out loud what most people already suspected: that 2022 broke him in ways the NFL never did.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ernie Accorsi — former Giants GM who set up team to win two Super Bowls — dead at 84
articles.summary: Ernie Accorsi was inducted into the Giants' Ring of Honor in 2016.
articles.body:
Ernie Accorsi — a football-lifer who helped the New York Giants win two Super Bowls — died Saturday, the team announced . He was 84.

In a statement, Giants president John Mara called Accorsi a "trusted advisor and dear friend."

"Ernie helped shape the course of New York Giants history through his vision, leadership and unwavering belief in building a championship organization. Beyond his accomplishments as a football executive, he was a trusted advisor and dear friend. His legacy will forever be part of the Giants, and he will be greatly missed."

While Accorsi's NFL journey began back in 1970, his biggest contributions to the game came as a member of the Giants. Accorsi initially joined the team as an assistant to the general manager before being promoted into the GM role in 1998.

The team reached the Super Bowl during the 2000 NFL season, where it fell to the Baltimore Ravens .

Following that loss, Accorsi was instrumental in building the Giants team that would eventually go on to win two Super Bowl titles. Between 2000 and 2006 — the year he retired — Accorsi acquired Eli Manning , Jeremy Shockey, Osi Umenyiora , Justin Tuck , Brandon Jacobs and Plaxico Burress through the draft, trades or free agency. All six of those players would play key roles in the team winning the Super Bowl during the 2007 and 2011 seasons.

Though Accorsi set up the majority of the roster that won it all in 2007, he was not technically a member of the Giants that season due to his retirement. The team, however, awarded Accorsi a championship ring for being the architect that brought that group together.

In 2016, the Giants honored Accorsi by inducting him into the team's Ring of Honor. Accorsi was inducted alongside Tuck and head coach Tom Coughlin — another member of the franchise who was recruited by Accorsi.

While all of those acquisitions played a massive role in the team's two Super Bowl wins, it was Accorsi's trade for Manning that stands above the rest. Entering the 2004 NFL Draft, Manning, Philip Rivers and Ben Roethlisberger were thought to be the three top quarterbacks in the draft. While Manning was expected to be the No. 1 overall pick, he did not want to play for the then-San Diego Chargers. Despite his pleas, the Chargers selected Manning No. 1 overall. It was initially unclear whether the team would force the issue or trade Manning away.

It didn't take long before that question was answered. The Giants — which picked No. 4 — grabbed Rivers moments later, and then agreed to swap the quarterbacks in a deal that shaped the future of multiple NFL franchises.

While both players put up excellent numbers over their careers, Manning led the Giants to two Super Bowl titles. Rivers never won a Super Bowl in his 18 years in the NFL. Both players, however, have a shot to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the future.

Manning also released a statement, thanking Accorsi for "making the trade and believing in me."

Coughlin, similarly, highlighted the Manning trade as Accorsi's biggest move.

"Ernie will always be remembered, and I say this out of great respect, he's the guy that made the trade for Eli Manning. That will go down in Giants history as one of the great moves of all time. Was it risky? Sure it was risky. Ernie did it. Shut the door, went in, he did it on his own. It was his move. He had followed Eli from the time Eli was a very young player at Ole Miss, and he was convinced that Eli was the franchise quarterback that the Giants needed. He was not going to be deterred. He saw an opportunity. I think both teams benefitted greatly from the decision, and Ernie pulled the trigger."

Ernie Accorsi spent decades working in football

Prior to joining the Giants, Accorsi served as the general manager of the Cleveland Browns , where he is credited for bringing franchise icon Bernie Kosar to the team. Prior to that, he was the general manager of the Baltimore Colts, and oversaw the team selecting — and then trading — John Elway. While Accorsi was the team's general manager at the time of that trade, it was team owner Jim Irsay — and not Accorsi — who was credited with trading Elway away.

Following his retirement from the Giants, Accorsi served as a consultant with a number of NFL teams, often assisting when those teams were looking for new general managers or coaches.

images.caption: UNITED STATES - JANUARY 03: New York Giants' General Manager Ernie Accorsi speaks at an end-of-season news conference at Giants Stadium. Accorsi insisted he never needed Eli Manning's last three games, or Sunday night's game-winning drive, to justify his faith in the rookie quarterback. (Photo by Linda Cataffo/NY Daily News Archive via Getty Images) (New York Daily News Archive via Getty Images)

articles.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed leaves field on backboard with his neck stabilized after contact to head on tackle
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's game against the New...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's game against the New York Jets .

The Packers quickly ruled him out with a neck injury.

Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele also left in the first quarter with a knee injury and was ruled out. The precise nature of Bako-Bewele's injury wasn't initially clear.

Reed carted off after being placed on backboard

Jets linebacker Demario Davis made contact to Reed's head with his shoulder pad on a hit in the first quarter. Reed was face down on the ground for a moment before rolling over to his back.

Medical staff immediately tended to Reed, and Packers players left their bench to surround their injured teammate as a cart came out.

Trainers put Reed on a backboard and stabilized his head before placing him on a cart. Reed was then taken off the field on the cart.

The precise nature and extent of Reed's injury weren't initially clear.

Reed, 26, is a fourth-year pro who's played his entire career for the Packers since being selected in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He's the No. 2 receiver on Green Bay 's depth chart behind Christian Watson .

Collarbone and foot injuries limited Reed to seven games in 2025. In his last full NFL season in 2024, Reed tallied 55 catches for 857 yards and 6 touchdowns. He posted three catches for 20 yards in Green Bay's Week 1 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .

images.caption: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed was taken off the field on a cart during a game against the New York Jets on Sunday. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase's first TD of the NFL season was sensational
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase got off to a slow start in Week 1 with just 2 catches for 12 yards. He'll be at the top of the highlight reels for Week 2.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase got off to a slow start in Week 1 with just two catches for 12 yards. He'll be at the top of the highlight reels for Week 2.

With the Bengals locked in a scoreless tie late in the first half against the Houston Texans , Chase got Cincinnati on the board in spectacular fashion.

On first-and-10 from the Houston 32-yard line, Chase ran a go route down the right sideline. Texans cornerback Derek Stingley had tight man coverage on Chase, but no help over the top.

Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow didn't hesitate to look Chase's way. He uncorked a deep pass toward the end zone.

Chase got just enough separation from Stingley as he tracked the ball, then turned around and snagged the ball out of the air, narrowly getting both feet down just inside the pylon. He secured possession with his right foot down, then got his left down in the end zone, just barely inbounds as he fell out of bounds.

Both of his feet were down as he had possession of the ball, and the Bengals struck first on the scoreboard for a 7-0 lead.

Chase is coming off a second consecutive season with 125-plus receptions that earned him his fifth Pro Bowl nod and third-career All-Pro selection. His slow start in Week 1 was notable, but no real reason for concern. As long as he's healthy, Chase remains one of the game's best receivers and most dangerous offensive weapons.

images.caption: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase got back into the end zone in style on Sunday. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

articles.title: Ja’Marr Chase’s ridiculous toe-tap TD might be best NFL catch this season
articles.summary: Only Ja'Marr Chase could make this touchdown catch
articles.body:
Tracking the ball downfield is an essential skill for a wide receiver in the NFL.

While all receivers need this trait, the elite players can make the impossible … possible.

Chase was on the other end of a deep throw downfield from quarterback Joe Burrow in the first half of Sunday's game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Houston Texans . With the Bengals offense facing a 1st-and-10 at the Houston 32-yard line, Burrow dropped deep in the pocket and targeted Chase on a vertical route.

Somehow, the receiver was able to track the ball, make a tough adjustment — more on how tough in a moment — and then drag his feet inbounds to complete the play for an improbable touchdown:

articles.title: Saquon Barkley returns to action after missing most of first half with stinger
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley was injured after just one carry in Week 2, but returned in the third quarter.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles had a rough first drive against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Things started off ominously, as star running back Saquon Barkley left the contest after just one carry due to a stinger.

After being tackled on the first carry of the game, Barkley went into the medical tent on the sideline and eventually jogged to the locker room.

He was initially deemed questionable to return due to a stinger and missed the rest of the first half due to the injury. But when the third quarter began, Barkley was back out on the field.

Things only got worse during the Eagles first drive, as quarterback Jalen Hurts threw an interception with the Eagles on the 8-yard line.

That interception was returned all the way to the opposing 10-yard line, setting up the Titans to score a touchdown a few plays later to take an early 7-0 lead.

Philadelphia battled back without Barkley in the first half, taking a 14-10 lead into halftime.

images.caption: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley left Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans after one carry and was diagnosed with a stinger. (Johnnie Izquierdo via Getty Images)
